title: Thread-pool starvation
sub: The server doesn't crash, it crawls
cards/0/body:
ASP.NET Core has no context, so .Result won't hang. But every such request holds a pool thread while it waits for the database.

Under load the threads run out, the pool adds new ones slowly, and responses stretch to seconds while the CPU is nearly idle.
cards/1/task: Add 16 requests with .Result and start the clock. How many threads are stuck, and how does the pool grow?
cards/2/task: Now the same 16 requests, but with await.
cards/3/q: What did the two exercises show?
cards/3/options/0: Blocking requests tie up threads and bloat the pool; with await the same 4 threads cope
cards/3/explain: Waiting without a thread is the main win of async on a server.
cards/4/q: Under load, responses lag by seconds and the CPU is nearly idle. What do you suspect first?
cards/4/explain: An idle CPU with growing latency means the threads exist but are stuck.
cards/5/body: In dotnet-counters, watch the pool's queue length and thread count. A growing queue with low CPU usage is a sure sign.
cards/5/deep: dotnet-counters monitor --counters System.Runtime shows ThreadPool Queue Length and ThreadPool Thread Count. In a process dump (dotnet-dump) during starvation you'll see dozens or hundreds of threads whose stacks end in .Result or Wait.
cards/6/q: What can cause pool starvation? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: .Result and .Wait() on tasks that query a database
cards/6/options/1: Thread.Sleep in code running on the pool
cards/6/options/2: A synchronous read from a slow disk in every request
cards/6/explain: Anything that holds a pool thread without doing work.
cards/7/q: A quick "fix": ThreadPool.SetMinThreads(500, 500). What do you think?
cards/7/options/0: It hides the symptom: threads still sit idle and eat memory; the cure is switching to await
cards/7/explain: Hundreds of waiting threads cost memory and context switches. The real cure is not blocking.
